subject.title: Feature: Pre-compaction agent notification, structured handoff window, and deferral mechanism

question: Should OpenClaw add an agent-controlled pre-compaction lifecycle contract, and which scope is allowed: warning only, structured handoff/checkpoint, bounded deferral, or no new surface?
rationale: The request crosses product UX, public config, persistence, and security boundaries because it changes when agents get extra write opportunities and whether compaction may be delayed after context pressure is detected.

options.title: Adopt warning and handoff only
options.body: Add a narrow opt-in warning plus structured handoff/checkpoint path while leaving agent-requested deferral out until authority semantics are settled.

options.title: Adopt full bounded deferral
options.body: Allow warning, handoff, and DEFER only with explicit max duration, audit trail, idempotent checkpoint matching, and approval expiry rules.

options.title: Decline new lifecycle surface
options.body: Keep memoryFlush, notifyUser, hooks, providers, and checkpoints as the supported compaction surfaces and route remaining needs to docs or plugins.

recommendation.title: Adopt warning and handoff only
recommendation.body: Add a narrow opt-in warning plus structured handoff/checkpoint path while leaving agent-requested deferral out until authority semantics are settled.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest current lifecycle behavior is pre-compaction memoryFlush, and history points to steipete as the strongest routing candidate for that boundary.
